sessionTitle: Using AI tools to teach old apps new tricks

announcements.name: Modernization Agent in the CLI is generally available
announcements.shortDescription: Orchestrates simultaneous assessments and migration plans across an entire app portfolio, with end-to-end automated Java and .NET framework upgrades
announcements.longDescription: The modernization agent, now generally available, is how you scale assessments and upgrades across your entire portfolio, operated from the CLI. It orchestrates multiple assessments and migration plans running simultaneously, then hands those plans off to developers who can execute and validate in their IDE. Java and .NET framework upgrades are now automated end-to-end straight from the agent CLI. It is part of GitHub Copilot modernization, built directly into GitHub Copilot.

announcements.name: Custom skills generally available
announcements.shortDescription: Lets teams encode their own migration patterns, internal libraries, and Azure best practices once and reuse them across the portfolio
announcements.longDescription: Custom skills, also generally available, let you customize and repeat tasks by encoding your team's specific migration patterns once and reusing them across your portfolio. The principle is write once, reuse at scale, so developers keep their business-specific logic and goals while still hitting enterprise-scale speed. It is part of GitHub Copilot modernization, available across editors, the CLI, the command center, and GitHub itself.

announcements.name: Command Center in Private Preview
announcements.shortDescription: A self-hostable portal giving a portfolio-level dashboard of modernization status, timelines, and comparable assessment reports
announcements.longDescription: The Command Center is a self-hostable portal that ships with the modernize CLI and provides a dashboard to see the status of your modernization across the organization. It surfaces phases such as how many applications have been assessed and planned, a project timeline showing start, deadline, and where the agents are today, and lets you share assessment reports company-wide. It also lets you compare between two assessment reports to make informed decisions about which migration looks best.

announcements.name: Rulebooks in Private Preview
announcements.shortDescription: Centrally encode governance, security, and architecture standards so agents modernize with guardrails and auto-generate compliance reports
announcements.longDescription: Rulebooks, announced in Private Preview, are where you encode your policy and architecture standards so agents modernize with guardrails. You can create a Rulebook inside the Command Center or in the modernize CLI, starting from a markdown file where you write rules, policies, security requirements, and hard boundaries the agents should never cross. Once generated, the Rulebook produces a charter with high-level principles (such as cloud-native authentication via default Azure credential, observability with OpenTelemetry, and approved SKUs like Azure Container Apps) that the agent sticks to when generating a plan.

announcements.name: Mainframe modernization added to GitHub Copilot Modernization
announcements.shortDescription: Reverse-engineers COBOL, JCL, and BMS into per-program documentation, then reimagines it as native Java with a native SQL data layer, delivered with partner experts
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft is introducing mainframe modernization as part of GitHub Copilot modernization to accelerate the overall mainframe modernization journey in a succinct, cautious, step-by-step manner. Starting in the modernize CLI, an assessment looks at source code such as COBOL, JCL, BMS, DB2, and VSAM files, identifies missing dependencies, and catches downstream issues early. It also documents the mainframe, providing a holistic executive-summary overview of what the application does, the user personas, functional modules, and key capabilities.

announcements.name: ASP.NET Web Forms and Aspire scenarios in Private Preview
announcements.shortDescription: Converts Web Forms apps to Blazor, adds Aspire orchestration, and deploys to Azure Container Apps
announcements.longDescription: The modernization agent can take an old ASP.NET Web Forms application (e.g., a default.aspx with components that run at server) and upgrade it to .NET 10, converting the entire Web Forms project into Blazor using the Blazor Server hosting model. Started from a Command Center plan or directly from the IDE, it works on a separate branch, containerizes the app, and moves it to a new pipeline rather than the old ASP.NET pipeline. Aspire, described as a code-first layer you add to your application, can then be added on top of the modernized app.

announcements.name: Azure Migrate to GitHub Copilot handoff
announcements.shortDescription: A seamless configuration-file handoff lets IT-led on-prem discovery flow into developer code assessment, with reports returned to Azure Migrate storage
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft now supports a seamless handoff between Azure Migrate and the GitHub Copilot Modernization Agent, since enterprise modernizations often start from on-prem infrastructure discovery rather than code assessment alone. Starting from Azure Copilot/Azure Migrate, IT teams assess production applications (seeing details like the web server, e.g., IIS), then choose "At Scale Code Assessment With Automated Report Upload" to generate a configuration file that bootstraps into the modernize CLI. The configuration includes information about Azure Migrate and where the assessment report should be sent back, so developers get reports in GitHub while IT professionals get reports returned to Azure Migrate Storage.
